scenes.title: Ground Guiding at Night
scenes.text: Ground guiding at night, with and without night vision devices. This simulation covers guiding the M1075A1 Palletized Load System truck after dark, using filtered visible light with the naked eye, and infrared light with the AN/PVS-14.

scenes.title: When You Need a Ground Guide
scenes.text: Army safety policy in AR 385-10 calls for a ground guide whenever a tactical vehicle backs up. Guides are also used in motor pools, assembly areas, tight spaces, and any time visibility is limited. Many units require two guides to back a vehicle the size of the PLS: one at the rear, and one at the front corner. Follow your unit SOP.

scenes.title: Brief Before You Move
scenes.text: Do brief before you move. The driver and ground guide agree on the signals, the type of light, and which side the guide will work from. The guide walks the route first, and checks for obstacles, wires, and ditches that the driver cannot see from the cab. Agree on what happens if a light fails or the guide drops out of sight: the driver stops.

scenes.title: Stay Where the Driver Can See You
scenes.text: Do stay where the driver can see you. Work from the driver's side rear corner, in the driver's mirror, at a safe distance from the truck. Never walk backward, never stand in the vehicle's path, and never stand between the truck and another object. Stay far enough out to the side that you can see the rear of the truck and the ground behind it at the same time.

scenes.title: Use Filtered Lights
scenes.text: Without NVDs, the guide uses two flashlights or lighted wands. Fit the filtered lens your unit specifies on the angle-head flashlight. Hold the lights where the driver sees them clearly in the mirror, without aiming them into the driver's eyes. Give the driver a moment to find your lights in the mirror before you start signaling.

scenes.title: Blind the Driver With White Light
scenes.text: Don't shine an unfiltered white light into the driver's mirror or face. The glare hides your signals and the ground around you. The driver's night vision can take many minutes to recover. If you need white light to check the ground, cover it with your hand, keep it pointed down, and turn away from the truck.

scenes.title: Disappear Into the Blind Spot
scenes.text: Don't drift into the blind spot. Directly behind the flatrack, the driver of a PLS cannot see you at all. During load handling, stay well clear of the hook arm, and the path of the flatrack. If you must cross behind the truck, signal stop first, and wait until the driver acknowledges.

scenes.title: Use IR Chemlights or Wands
scenes.text: With NVDs, the guide uses infrared chemlights or IR-filtered wands. Through the PVS-14 they glow clearly. To the naked eye, they are invisible. Anyone not wearing NVDs, including a crew member or a nearby vehicle, cannot see your signals. Brief this ahead of time, so everyone knows which lights are in use.

scenes.title: Signal Big and Slow
scenes.text: Do use the standard signals from TC 21-60. Make them large, slow, and inside the driver's view. A small, quick movement is easy to miss through a forty-degree tube. Hold the stop signal until the truck is fully stopped.

scenes.title: Aim IR Light at the Driver
scenes.text: Don't aim an IR flashlight or illuminator straight at the driver. Through night vision, it blooms just like a headlight, and washes out the image. Keep IR lights low, and point them toward the ground between signals. One bright source can also trigger the tube's automatic gain, and darken everything else in the driver's view.

scenes.title: Guide on NVDs: Keep Your Distance
scenes.text: When the ground guide also wears a PVS-14, the same limits apply. Depth perception is poor, so keep extra distance from the truck, move slowly, and watch your footing on uneven ground. Scan the ground before you step, and signal stop early, long before the truck gets close.

scenes.title: Driver: Lost Sight? Stop.
scenes.text: Drivers, if you lose sight of the ground guide or the lights, stop immediately and wait. Take directions from only one guide, but stop for anyone who signals stop. Once you stop, hold the brakes, and wait for the guide to reappear and signal before you move again.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.text: To recap. Do: brief the plan, stay visible on the driver's side, use filtered light without NVDs and infrared light with them, signal big and slow, and stop when sight is lost. Don't: blind the driver with white or infrared light, stand in the path or the blind spot, or assume people without NVDs can see your IR signals.

scenes.title: Guide Them In
scenes.text: Backing accidents at night are preventable. Verify these procedures against AR 385-10, TC 21-60, AR 600-55, and your unit SOP.
